title: A gentle measure helps release habit

captions.physics: Considering change’s consequences for both people

meaning: Honest, considerate care helps you experience a familiar arrangement ending without requiring the same pace of saying goodbye.
text: A familiar arrangement may end before feelings have caught up. In the physical position of Anahata, Justice expresses care through honest decisions about help and the consequences of change for both people. Temperance in energy brings a wish to reconcile different needs and find a considerate measure for transition. Death in emotions offers an experience of ending: something familiar will not return in its former shape. Warmth may come from having that loss acknowledged without demands for immediate happiness or attempts to preserve the past at any cost.

Suppose you clear a room of a large desk that you used together for a long time. One person already wants more space while the other feels sad about parting with a familiar place. You divide the tasks fairly and leave time to choose a small keepsake. **A gentle transition allows different feelings about one ending.** The desk leaves, but an important memory need not be declared useless for the sake of new convenience.

Trying to soften change can prolong parting with an unnecessary arrangement or make sadness an inconvenient obstacle. The measure you found then supports only one person. Care stays honest when what has ended really ends, while feelings are not hurried in the name of mutual benefit. You can agree on an action now without promising to feel exactly the same at the same time.
